bib.title: OpenAssistant Conversations - Democratizing Large Language Model Alignment
bib.venue: NeurIPS 2023 Track on Datasets and Benchmarks (arXiv v2)

question: Can a fully open, human-written and human-ranked assistant conversation corpus be built by crowd-sourcing and used to align open LLMs with SFT and RLHF?
hypothesis: Models fine-tuned on OpenAssistant Conversations improve over their base models; ranking human-written (not policy) replies may explain why RLHF gains over SFT are small.
contributions: Release OpenAssistant Conversations (OASST1): 161,443 messages, 35 languages, 461,292 quality ratings, >10,000 complete trees, from >13,500 volunteers
Release SFT, reward and RLHF models based on Pythia, LLaMA and Falcon
Data collection platform, guidelines and moderation pipeline released under a permissive licence
Analysis of dataset, toxicity, contributor demographics and ethics

method.summary: Volunteers write prompts, assistant and prompter replies, label and rank replies in a web app that grows conversation trees one task at a time. Ranks from K independent rankers are merged with Tideman's ranked pairs. The data trains SFT models, reward models (pairwise loss) and PPO (trlx) policies on Pythia, LLaMA, Falcon.
method.task: assistant-style SFT, reward modelling and RLHF from crowd-sourced conversation trees

datasets.name: OpenAssistant Conversations (OASST1)
datasets.size: 161,443 messages (91,829 prompter, 69,614 assistant) in 66,497 trees; 10,968 complete trees with 92,365 messages; 52,159 trees are a single initial prompt; 8,576 synthetic messages (152,867 human); 461,292 quality ratings; 35 languages
datasets.split: SFT mix config uses val_split 0.05 for oasst_export; recommended variant is completed trees
datasets.source: crowd-sourced from >13,000 volunteers (13,500 in abstract) via web app; released at huggingface.co/OpenAssistant/oasst1 under a fully permissive licence
datasets.preprocessing: spam/guideline labels, moderator deletion, removal of ChatGPT-like phrases ('as a large language model'); deleted messages not exported; ranks merged by Tideman ranked pairs

datasets.name: Falcon sft-mix extra datasets
datasets.size: vicuna 50% (16963), code_alpaca 50% (9510), oa_wiki_qa_bart_10000row (9434), grade_school_math_instructions (8351), dolly15k (14250), oasst_export (29899)

datasets.name: LMEH subset (BoolQ, PIQA, HellaSwag, WinoGrande, ARC-e, ARC-c, OBQA)

training.objective: SFT: LM loss on assistant tokens only (prompt tokens masked). RM: LM head replaced by linear layer giving scalar r_theta for last reply; pairwise loss -1/C(K,2) E[log sigma(r(x,yw)-r(x,yl))], optional regulariser. PPO via trlx with per-token KL penalty from SFT model
training.steps: Pythia SFT 7k steps (name pythia-12b-sft-v8-7k-steps); LLaMA RLHF 5k steps (name only)
training.regularisation: KL penalty in PPO; optional RM value regulariser
training.compute: Redmond AI provided training compute; amount not stated

other.rm_eval: accuracy at ordering pairs of replies of different rank on held-out validation set
other.ppo_prompts: assistant replies generated to unanswered questions

inference.samples: not stated for Table 1; political compass: multiple samples with majority vote
inference.prompting: standardized prompts for political compass (text not given)

metrics.name: LMEH
metrics.definition: average over BoolQ, PIQA, HellaSwag, WinoGrande, ARC-e, ARC-c, OBQA

metrics.name: VEL
metrics.definition: Vicuna Elo Rank, LLM-judged Elo ranking

metrics.name: Detoxify categories
metrics.definition: mean automated toxicity per category over messages

eval.protocol: Evaluations run externally with FastEval, hosted on a continually updated leaderboard; single numbers, no seeds or significance tests; instruction benchmarks omitted for base models

results.claim: Dataset size: messages, languages, ratings, volunteers.
results.quote: we release OpenAssistant Conversations, a human-generated, human-annotated assistant-style conversation corpus consisting of 161,443 messages in 35 different languages, annotated with 461,292 quality ratings
Of the 66,497 total conversation trees, we consider 10,968 complete
results.note: Abstract says over 10,000 complete trees; 52,159 trees are only a single initial prompt.

results.claim: Falcon-40B SFT (top1) beats Falcon-40B base on LMEH.
Pythia-12B SFT does not improve LMEH over base.
results.note: Contradicts the 'consistently outperforming' claim in the text for this pair.

results.claim: LLaMA-30B SFT edges LLaMA-65B base on LMEH.
LLaMA-30B RLHF Vicuna Elo is higher than SFT (979) but OpenAI Evals and HumanEval are lower (0.52/0.20 SFT vs 0.51/0.15 RLHF).
RLHF outperforms SFT on some benchmarks and not others.
results.quote: RLHF outperforms SFT in some benchmarks, but not in others.

results.claim: Open models close to ChatGPT in some benchmarks; large gaps in others (gpt-3.5-turbo HumanEval 0.72, OAIE 0.87, VEL 1110; best OASST HumanEval 0.20).
Authors' hypothesis: RLHF gains over SFT are smaller than InstructGPT's because the RM was trained on human-written replies, not SFT-model samples.
results.quote: We hypothesize that the difference in data collection for the reward model could at least partially explain this gap.
results.note: Untested; authors plan to collect rankings on their own SFT outputs.

results.claim: Detoxify toxicity is higher for deleted than retained messages.
results.setup: deleted messages, 3422 sampled, Detoxify supported languages

results.claim: Over 95% of 270 survey respondents glad to have contributed (81.11% strongly agree, 14.44% agree).
results.table: Table 3, row Overall glad I contributed, Strongly agree

results.claim: 89.1% of annotators identify as male, median age 26.
results.quote: Specifically, 89.1% of the annotators identify as male, with a median age of 26.

limits: RM trained on human-written replies, not policy samples; RLHF gains inconsistent (Sec 7)
Annotators 89.1% male, median age 26; power users over-represented
Dataset may contain unsafe content and residual ChatGPT-generated text
Training hyperparameters, compute and seeds not in paper (deferred to GitHub); benchmark numbers are single runs from an external leaderboard
Survey is a self-selected Discord sample (270 responses)
Authors advise research use only; models susceptible to prompt injection
